No it definitely helps. In my experience, therapy first forces you to mentally come to terms with things that are painful or that you have been avoiding out of fear. Then, it gives you tools to minimize the affect of that thing in your life, and helps you learn how to approach your life with a more healthy, balanced perspective. Obviously, a good therapist is better than a bad therapist. But talking to any person trained in talk therapy can be useful. Try to seek out someone who specializes in whatever it is you are struggling with.

It's true that you could get the same benefits from self help (have you ever tried listening to podcasts focused on mental health/self healing? Tara Brach is a good place to start), but depending on the amount of damage that whatever it is that making you depressed/angry/addicted/grieved in the first place is, you are likely to revert without someone guiding you.

Unless you have a very wise confidant/mentor to turn to, I don't recommend seeking help from a friend or family member. These people, while truly well meaning, can often give very poor advice or won't give you their honest evaluation of your situation because they don't want to cause more pain for you in the moment, even if it is necessary for your personal growth. It can also burden personal relationships and could eventually make that person resent you for leaning on them so heavily.
